claims: E15 is a gasoline blend containing 15% ethanol and 85% gasoline.
E15 is often marketed as Unleaded 88.
E10 is a standard 10% blend.
E15 has an octane rating of 88.
Regular E10 has an octane rating of 87.
Summer sales of E15 are now permitted via EPA emergency waivers.
E15 is typically 5 to 15 cents cheaper per gallon than E10, say sources like this YouTube video.
E15 reduces greenhouse gas emissions by up to 46% compared to straight gasoline according to this YouTube video.
E15 is derived from corn.
Ethanol has less energy than gasoline.
E15 is approved for model year 2001 and newer cars, light-duty trucks, and flex-fuel vehicles.
E15 is prohibited for motorcycles.
E15 is prohibited for heavy-duty vehicles.
E15 is prohibited for boats.
E15 is prohibited for all-terrain vehicles.
E15 is sold at over 3,000 stations in 31 states, says the Department of Energy.
E15 was traditionally banned in summer due to volatility concerns.
The EPA has initiated emergency waivers for nationwide summer sales of E15, note 12News and Congress.gov.
Fuel Ox notes that E15 can cause rubber hose degradation.
Fuel Ox notes that E15 can cause plastic component damage.
Fuel Ox notes that E15 can cause increased corrosion.
